frames.reason: ALIGNMENT: all four frames show ORE 730, GAS 166, SUPPLY 24/30, CLOCK 00:05, SURVEYOR QUEUED, Command Core 1 selected 1800/1800 (-70 . 66), with the same camera and object positions. Repeats within each arm look identical, so no action/debris/state difference is being blamed on rendering. WORLD: AFTER lifts the crushed dark floor (top-left x0-400,y50-300 from near-black to mid grey; plateau from saturated brown-tan to lighter khaki) and the grid stays readable. Building tops and infantry become paler blue-grey, but dark sides and contact shadows (barracks base x673-700,y440-490, Command Core base y420-445, building feet) stay dark and read better against the lighter floor. I see no new flat or clipped white patch. Teal accents (barracks roof, Command Core core glow, crystals) are more saturated, not just brighter. The building rings (Command Core, barracks, left and top buildings) are visibly bolder bright cyan with a dark rim, versus BEFORE's thin teal line. Mint bars with a dark underlay remain over all five bar sites. The direction (lifted neutral base, softer shoulder, saturated accents, grounded shadows) matches the ThreeNative last-post to now move toward the Unreal panels on the L9 boards, so this is not brightness alone. HUD: black backing raises text, border, HP-bar and queue-chip contrast (teal fill vs black remainder is more distinct). All text is readable; the clipped SURVEYOI chip label is unchanged from BEFORE. The new hint strip covers only floor/grid: nothing visible BEFORE sits under x944-1264,y634-664 (PAUSE y>=680 and pool y>=703 are below it). Behind the BEFORE panels in this pose there is only floor grid, so no through-panel cue is lost. The dark plateau surround is authored terrain present in BEFORE and is now more legible, not a new halo. I see no grain, banding, ghosting or edge artifact at native view. No hostile units or order markers appear in this pose.

frames.reason: ALIGNMENT: all four frames show ORE 730, GAS 150, SUPPLY 23/30, CLOCK 00:03, Vanguard Assault infantry, 10 selected, 100/100 (-57 . 49), IDLE, with the same camera and positions. Repeats within each arm look identical. AFTER lifts the floor and plateau and reveals grid and terrain shading in the formerly dark upper area. The top pool reads more clearly as water (more saturated teal, same soft rim). Buildings keep a pale-top / dark-side / dark-contact-shadow structure (barracks base x418-440,y670-705, Command Core base, infantry feet) with no flat or clipped white. Command Core and barracks rings are bolder cyan with a dark rim. The infantry cluster keeps all its stacked mint and dark bars and its 1 px cyan arcs at the same extents; bars are paler mint, arcs brighter cyan. THROUGH-PANEL CHECK: BEFORE showed faintly through the teal strike-group panel the Command Core's left body and ring arc (x258-304,y575-668), the start of its dark bar (x290-304,y569) and two small units (x135-175,y583-625). In both AFTER repeats the ring is brighter and the Command Core facets are visible. The two units remain identifiable as dark silhouettes with amber cargo bits against the near-black backing, comparable to BEFORE's pale ghost. The dark bar is traceable x~290-362, with the 14 px under the panel faint in both arms. I could not confirm any of these as fainter, but they are the lowest-contrast items in the pose. The hint strip covers only plateau floor/grid; no cue visible BEFORE lies under x944-1264,y634-664. HUD text, buttons and bars are more legible on black. I see no grain, banding, ghosting, floating base or new edge artifact. No hostile units, order markers or damaged/partial bars appear in this pose.

reason: Both assigned poses move toward the Unreal L9 panels by more than brightness: a lifted but neutral floor with readable grid, retained facet and contact-shadow structure, more saturated accents and bolder faction/selection rings, with no clipped white. The gameplay cues (bars, rings, infantry cluster, small units, minimap marker/frustum/blob, queue chip and all HUD text) are present at identical positions in both repeats per arm, and none is confirmed weaker. The near-black HUD backing and the new hint strip hide nothing that was visible BEFORE in these two poses. This is a two-pose subset leaf, so it does not establish whole-kit IMPROVEMENT by itself. The open contrast watch is not closed by this review; see contrastWatchDecision. I credit nothing to the resolution pin.
limitations: By-eye review only: the Read tool gave no zoom, pixel diff or measurement, and coordinates are +/-3 px. Thin 1-3 px cues are near the viewer's resolution. That matters most for the stacked infantry bars and 1 px arcs in the survives cluster (x540-640,y540-620) and for the 14 px of Command Core bar under the strike-group panel. The two small units behind that panel (x135-175,y583-625) are low-contrast in both arms; I judged them comparable but did not measure. TEMPORAL CRITERION UNVERIFIED: these are static endpoint frames, so I say nothing about exposure settling, pumping or flicker, adaptation, ring/grid shimmer in motion, FPS or audio. Matching repeats establish only endpoint repeatability. No hostile units, order/attack markers, damage feedback or low-health partial-bar states appear in either pose, so enemy colours and those cues are not assessable. The only genuine partial fill is the rts-train queue chip. The hint-strip check is pose-specific: it covers only floor/grid here. The L9 comparison is directional: the RTS has no sky or specular spheres. I used the two mixed boards honestly, taking only the far-right Unreal panel of harness-L9-source.png and the right Unreal column of harness-L9-full-sun60.png as the target and treating the other panels as ThreeNative. AI-attack watch evidence comes from the three supplied JSONs and was not re-measured; I did not open AI-attack frames or crops. The teal-to-near-black HUD change is the declared intent and is judged and credited for legibility only, not as a palette improvement. No benefit is attributed to the resolution pin, and I did not compare AUTO. Whole-kit IMPROVEMENT still depends on the other five poses and the final reviewer. I re-read the four survives raws once for the through-panel check.
contrastWatchDecision: No WHOLE actual bar, ring or infantry cue is confirmed weaker in rts-train or survives. rts-train: the five bar sites (top building y~235, Command Core x548-618/y~343, left building y~381, barracks y~408, infantry cluster x818-853/y~317) and the four building rings are present at identical positions and extents in all four frames. AFTER bars are paler mint with a dark underlay and the rings are bolder bright cyan with a dark rim, so they read at least as strongly as BEFORE's sage/teal. The infantry bar sits above the heads over floor, so there is no pale-head overlap in this pose. survives: the selected 10-unit cluster x540-640,y540-620 keeps its stacked mint and dark bars (y543-577) and 1 px cyan arcs (y583-620) at the same extents in both repeats. The building/vehicle bars (x337-408/y461, x465-502/y498, x568-604/y499, x441-511/y634) and the Command Core and barracks rings are present, and the dark segments now sit on a lighter floor with more separation. Under the near-black panel, the Command Core ring and bar start and the two small units (x135-175,y583-625) stay identifiable. Effect of dark backing: I see a thin dark rim on the large rings and under the building bars, but I cannot resolve its extent on the 3 px stacked infantry bars at native view. Residual uncertainty, not confirmed: the supplied AI-attack numbers (eight-bar cluster) show a real but modest fall in relative lightness contrast on the lifted floor. The sampled bar L* step goes 25.87 to 20.75 and its Y ratio 2.829 to 2.021. The ring-edge pixel L* step goes 14.93/15.26 to 11.09/8.83 and its Y ratio 1.93/1.95 to 1.49/1.38. Over the same samples, absolute Y separation rises for the bar and for the run1 ring pixel, falls for the run2 ring pixel (0.115 vs 0.135/0.139), and RGB distance rises for all. No threshold was predeclared. The same mechanism plausibly applies to mint bars crossing the palest infantry bodies and to the 1 px infantry arcs in the survives cluster. At 1280x720 I cannot see them fainter, but without zoom or measurement this review does not close the watch.
